description_full: UMB Financial Corporation operates as a bank holding company that provides banking services and asset servicing in the United States and internationally. The company operates through three segments: Commercial Banking, Institutional Banking, and Personal Banking. The Commercial Banking segment provides commercial loans and credit cards; commercial real estate financing; letters of credit; loan syndication, and consultative services; various business solutions including asset-based lending, mezzanine debt, and minority equity investment; and treasury management service, such as depository service, account reconciliation, cash management tool, accounts payable and receivable solution, electronic fund transfer and automated payment, controlled disbursement, lockbox service, and remote deposit capture service. The Institutional Banking segment offers banking, fund, asset management, and healthcare services to institutional clients; fund administration and accounting, investor services and transfer agency, alternative investment services, fixed income sales, trading and underwriting, and corporate trust and escrow services, as well as institutional custody services. This segment also provides healthcare payment solutions, including custodial service for health saving accounts and private label, multipurpose debit cards to insurance carriers, third-party administrators, software companies, employers, and financial institutions. The Personal Banking segment offers deposit account, retail credit card, private banking, installment loan, home equity line of credit, residential mortgage, as well as internet banking, ATM network, private banking, brokerage and insurance service, and investment advisory, trust, and custody services. It operates through a network of branches and offices. The company was founded in 1913 and is headquartered in Kansas City, Missouri.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 5K people. financial_summary: UMB Financial Corporation is a large-cap financial services business with a $10.2B market cap on $2.7B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +22% over the past three years and +12% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 41% against a 9% cost of capital — a 31-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $978M in free cash flow — roughly 37 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.46× so those profits are backed by real cash.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 0.6× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Net dilution runs at 0.8% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 5.3% of the shares.

Insiders are net sellers (73% sell ratio, net $4.5M) — the people closest to the business are reducing their personal stake
Credit cycles and regulatory capital — losses accumulate invisibly in good years and appear all at once, and the time to worry is when underwriting standards are loosest.
Fintech disintermediation — neobanks, embedded finance, and blockchain rails are unbundling the fee streams that traditional banks took for granted.
Interest rate regime shifts — a rapid move in rates can invert the yield curve, crush bond portfolios, and trigger deposit flight simultaneously.

sect: Its 33% operating margin is roughly in line with the Financial Services median (29%).
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.27x).
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+8.1% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.02 across 514 companies in the universe; the top four hold 20% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 21% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 11% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 13% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 25% and a beta of 0.87, it moves roughly with the market.
About $78.5M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 39% in the 2020 crash, 29% in the 2022 bear market and 50% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 63% below its DCF fair value of $359, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 34%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $298 to $448 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 27% below its 10-year median.
The 16 covering analysts target $161 on average, 20% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 41% clears the cost of capital of 9.2% by 31pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.83).
It converts 37% of revenue into free cash flow.
As a lender it runs a net interest margin of 3.28% and an efficiency ratio of 48% (lean).
It earns a 9% return on equity.
hlth: CET1 capital of 11.8% sits comfortably above the ~7% regulatory minimum with buffer.
Non-performing loans are 0.34% of the book, a clean credit profile.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 21.8% over 3 years, 15.5% over 5 years and 11.7% over 10 years, so growth is accelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 15%).
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 15.0% on average.
Analysts expect 4.3% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own 5.3%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 98%.
Insider trading is two-way: 4 purchases and 11 sales over the past year, net $4.5M sold.
Net share issuance leaves shareholder yield negative (-0.8%), diluting holders.
The share count has grown 9.4% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
It has paid a dividend for 39 consecutive years, raising it 17.6% a year over the last five.
people: With about 5,222 employees, each generates about $508K of revenue, in line with the Financial Services median, and revenue has grown 9.6% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $187K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $4.9M (10x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (3/10, lower is better).

profile.head: Watch: no strong case either way.
